citations.narrative:
Female Alaskan Klee-Kai (tag #50) has the toes of her left front foot trapped in the raised wire flooring. The inspector
observed the dog try to pull her foot from the flooring but was unable to do so. The facility representative was able to
extract the toes and free the dog's foot from the flooring. Flooring that entraps a dog's toes or feet may cause injury, may
prevent the dog from accessing food and water, or may prevent the dog from escaping aggressive cage mates.
One enclosure, containing 5 dogs, is constructed with raised wire flooring. The flooring along the west wall of the
enclosure is not attached to the framework and has begun to bend upward. The flooring was also cut in a manner that has
created numerous sharp points which are also bending slightly upwards. Sharp points and flooring that is not solidly
attached to the framework could increase the risk of injury to the dogs.
Primary enclosures must be constructed and maintained so that they protect the dogs from injury. The licensee must alter
the flooring in a manner that eliminates the risk of entrapment or injury. The licensee must ensure that all enclosure
flooring is safe for the dogs at all times.
To be corrected by: Corrected at time of inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
